events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
Cancellation was made by the rider, so the fee can only stand via NS-0 → NS-4 [F2][NS-0]. NS-4 makes a rider cancellation chargeable only if it occurs more than 3 minutes after matching; here acceptance was at 14:05:00 and cancellation at 14:07:55, i.e. 175 s (2 min 55 s), which is inside the 3-minute grace window [F2][NS-4]. The trace settles this element as failed (✗), and a rider cancellation within 3 minutes "are not chargeable" [F2][NS-4].

Independently, no driver-side no-show basis exists: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded arrival at the pickup point [F3][F4], and the driver never came within 200 m, the closest approach being 1685 m [F1][NS-1]. The driver's statement that he "was on his way" [F9] is a statement only and is contradicted by the GPS record, which controls [F1]; it also cannot convert a rider cancellation into a driver-side no-show cancellation under NS-1.

The driver's traffic remark [F8] and the NASSIM ROAD speed-band 3 record [F10] do not help: band 3 is not a band 1/2 record, and no incident was recorded on the route in the trip window [F11][RD-4]. Weather was fair [F12], so no reasonable-cause detour issue arises.

Amount: the fee on record is $6.61 [F5], with surge 1.0× [F6]; full refund = $6.61 [F5][NS-4]. The rider's clean dispute history [F13] is not relied on for the outcome; the driver's upheld no-show profile entries [F14] do not alone decide anything and, since no violation and no refundable overcharge arises against the driver, RD-6 is not triggered, so no account flag.
